Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a clinician-ready document with a dated historical chronology of my January–April 2027 right-ankle running rehabilitation, covering the initial run-walk restart and the later April continuous-run block with session structure, spacing, during-session and later-that-day symptom checks, and following-day walking and stair observations; make clear this is history, not current clearance or a new progression recommendation.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Right Ankle Running Rehabilitation Chronology — January–April 2027", "body": "# Right Ankle Running Rehabilitation Chronology

**Period covered:** January–April 2027  
**Purpose:** Historical summary for clinician review; compiled from the recorded rehabilitation and running log.

> **Historical record only.** This chronology documents past instructions, sessions, and reported responses. It is **not current medical clearance**, does not establish present status, and is **not a new progression recommendation**. Please confirm the current plan and any activity limits with the treating clinician.

## January: reassessment and run–walk restart

- **January 8 — rehabilitation follow-up:** The clinician documented no swelling, instability, gait change, or sign of acute bone injury, and recorded an assessment of load-sensitive irritation of the medial ankle tendon. The previous two-session, 40-minute running baseline was suspended. The recorded restart prerequisites were 14 consecutive days without focal pain and a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk with a symptom-free following day. The prescribed restart was two nonconsecutive sessions weekly, 20 minutes alternating four-minute easy runs and one-minute walks; continuous running was to await clinical review after six symptom-free run–walk sessions. Ankle-and-calf strengthening was to continue three times weekly.
- **January 23–24 — brisk-walk prerequisite:** A 30-minute brisk walk was reported symptom-free during the walk, later that day, and through the following day; no gait change was reported. The record states that the 14-day symptom-free prerequisite had been completed.
- **January 26 — first restart session:** Completed the prescribed 20-minute four-minute-run/one-minute-walk pattern. No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during the session or later that day. Ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free through January 27.
- **January 30 — second session:** Same 20-minute interval structure. Later records group this session among the six symptom-free sessions; no symptom or following-day concern was reported.

## February: completion of first interval block, then longer run–walk intervals

- **February 2, 6, 10, and 13:** Completed the 20-minute alternating four-minute easy-run/one-minute-walk sessions. The February 2, 6, 10, and 13 records report no focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during or later that day, and no following-day symptoms; the February 2 check included ordinary walking and stairs through February 3. Together with January 26 and 30, these completed six symptom-free sessions.
- **February 19 — clinical review:** Following review of those six nonconsecutive 20-minute sessions and their following-day checks, the recorded plan permitted two nonconsecutive 25-minute sessions weekly alternating nine-minute easy runs and one-minute walks. Six symptom-free sessions at this level were required before continuous running; the former 40-minute baseline remained suspended.
- **February 21, 24, and 28; March 3, 7, and 10 — 25-minute run–walk block:** Six nonconsecutive sessions, each alternating nine-minute easy runs with one-minute walks for 25 minutes. The log reports no focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change; session, later-that-day, and following-day checks were symptom-free. Ordinary walking and stairs were specifically noted symptom-free through March 11 after the March 10 session. Strengthening continued three times weekly; no third weekly run was added.

## March: clinical transition to continuous running and a symptom recurrence

- **March 15 — clinical check:** After the six symptom-free 25-minute run–walk sessions, the recorded clearance was for two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly, with ankle-and-calf strengthening and session-plus-following-day checks continued. The record specifically says that 40-minute runs and a third weekly session were not cleared.
- **March 17 and 21 — first two continuous sessions:** Each was 30 minutes easy and continuous; sessions were nonconsecutive. Neither produced focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during the run or later that day. Ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free through the following-day checks on March 18 and 22. Strengthening continued; no third run was added.
- **March 14 — earlier reported recurrence:** A separate running-log entry reports focal ache on the inside of the right ankle beginning at about minute 31; running stopped at minute 33. The clinic requested reassessment before further running. Ordinary walking was reported without recurrence, swelling, instability, or gait change. **This entry predates the March 15 clearance in the available records, so its relationship to the March 15 continuous-running block is not clear from the chronology.**
- **March 24 — 30-minute run entry:** A subsequent log entry reports a 30-minute continuous easy run with no focal pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during or later that day; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through March 25. A March 26 reassessment record says running had been placed back at two nonconsecutive 30-minute easy sessions weekly after the March 14 recurrence, and that further progression awaited clinical follow-up. The available entries do not fully clarify the authorization/timing of the March 24 run relative to the reassessment; this is noted rather than inferred.
- **March 26 — PT reassessment:** Focal inside-right-ankle ache had not recurred during ordinary walking; no swelling, instability, or gait change was reported. The record maintained two nonconsecutive 30-minute easy sessions weekly, ongoing strengthening, and session-plus-following-day checks; focal pain or gait change ended a run. Further progression was to wait for clinical follow-up.

## April: 30-minute block, then two 35-minute trials

- **April 4, 7, 11, and 14 — 30-minute continuous easy runs:** The corrected running log lists these four sessions, at two nonconsecutive sessions per week. No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change was reported during the runs or later that day; ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free through each following-day check, including April 15. Strengthening continued three times weekly. No 40-minute run or third weekly session was attempted. (An earlier preliminary note listed different dates; the April 15 correction is used here.)
- **April 16 — follow-up and duration-only trial authorization:** The clinician authorized two 35-minute easy lake-trail trials on April 19 and April 26, while maintaining two nonconsecutive sessions weekly and keeping the other weekly run at 30 minutes during the trial period. The recorded condition was that both trials and their following-day checks remain symptom-free before 35 minutes becomes the standard duration. Focal pain or gait change was to end a session and return running to 30 minutes; recurrent focal pain required follow-up.
- **April 19 — first 35-minute trial; April 20 check:** Reported symptom-free during the run and later that day, without focal pain, gait change, swelling, or instability; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through April 20.
- **April 26 — second 35-minute trial; April 27 check:** Reported symptom-free during the run and later that day, without focal pain, gait change, swelling, or instability; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through April 27. The record states that the two-trial progression was completed and that two nonconsecutive 35-minute easy sessions weekly became the recorded baseline beginning April 27. Strengthening continued, with no third weekly session. The session-plus-following-day check remained in the record.

## Documentation notes

- For the sessions explicitly documented as symptom-free, the record generally tracks symptoms **during the session**, **later that day**, and **through the following day**; following-day observations specifically include ordinary walking and stair use where noted above.
- Entries refer to focal pain at the inside/medial right ankle and to gait change, swelling, and instability as monitored symptoms. No current examination findings or present-day symptom status are established by this historical summary.
- Dates and details above reflect the available records.
